design.reason: The finding survives on execution and on design. Execution: I reran repro_scan.py on d3_names. The results match the finding exactly. host.docker.internal:11434, api.internal:8080, nas.home.arpa and ollama:11434 each get D3 contradiction with reason net_external_host. svc.default.svc.cluster.local is 内 and api.example.com is 矛. Design: §7.3 names the local class only as "localhost / private / loopback", and it defines "private" only for IP addresses (through ipaddress.is_private). Nothing defines it for host names. I found no D number, O item, D19 K1-K7 entry or preregistration text that settles this. D56 (c3a8c0c) introduced _host_class, and taking in `.local`, which is not in the rule text, was an unrecorded implementation choice. Open question O23 #4 did list "the definition of an external host (private range / localhost / env-derived hosts)" as a decision point, but the resolution chose (a) without defining names. evidence/review/explore_r3plus.json records host.docker.internal → external 矛 as "a gap in the rule, D3 only". That note was only a record under the old §2 scope ("D3/D4-only errors are recorded, not fixed"). D62 and review_plan §7.5 withdrew that scope, so the note is not an intended design decision. The finding also does not ask to add frozen vocabulary (sink / entry / weak reason), because the host classification is not one of those vocabularies. Re-deriving the expected output: RFC 6761 `.localhost`, RFC 6762 `.local`, RFC 8375 `home.arpa` and the ICANN 2024 reservation of `.internal` are all standards-defined names that do not resolve on the public internet. Treating them as "private" for the same reason `.local` is treated that way is consistent. So 内 is the right result for `.internal`, `home.arpa` and host.docker.internal. For single-label names, "always local" does not follow because of ccTLD apex records, so 不 under principle 2-a is the consistent result. The finding itself allows this. Uncertainty: because the rule never defines "private" for names, this is closer to a gap in the rule than a clear implementation defect. The fix must come from the student defining the term in §7.3 first, not from looking at the counts. Impact estimate: in v2 run13 all 37 D3 net_external_host cases were public hosts (kakao/feishu/pushover/dartmouth; decisions.md:3035), so the v2 count probably does not change. The corpus-wide string counts (375 etc.) include tests and vendored code, so they are only an upper bound. Severity stays low.

My own extra case, metadata.google.internal (it resolves to 169.254.169.254), is also 矛 net_external_host. That is inconsistent with the IP rule: the literal 169.254.169.254 is classified local through is_link_local, so the same destination gets opposite verdicts depending on whether it is written as a name or an IP. The claim does not depend on anything specific to v2 or v3. It follows from §7.3's words "localhost / private / loopback" and from the standards: RFC 6761 .localhost, RFC 6762 .local, RFC 8375 home.arpa, and ICANN reserving .internal in 2024. The implementation accepts only .local and rejects the others with the same standing, which is an asymmetric choice. On the design lens: §7.3 does not define private for names, O23 #4 and D56 say nothing about this, and review_plan §5 does not list it as a known design decision. So this is not a restatement of a decision. On generality: a general fix exists (see notes). The most natural naive fix, treating a host with no '.' as 不 before the IP parse, would break bare IPv6 loopback http://[::1]/x, which is currently correctly 内 (I checked with repro_scan). The finding's fix_sketch already avoids this by limiting the rule to names that are not IPs. Suffix false matches do not happen: x.internal.example.com stays 矛 because endswith('.internal') is false. Concatenation and f-string hosts never become a truncated dotless constant: 'https://api' + p is MODEL, and BASE + '.example.com' is net_host_unknown. So the dotless → 不 rule does not turn a correct 矛 into a mistake. Doubts: (1) Whether .internal and home.arpa count as private is a choice about how to define the rule, and the student makes it. The finding's wording "定義が無い" is accurate, and it is fair to call this "the implementation made a narrow choice before the rule was written", not a mistake in the rule. generality.notes: General fix: first write down in §7.3 how private is defined for names, and commit that before changing the implementation. (a) Local names, taken from the standards: localhost / *.localhost (RFC 6761), *.local (RFC 6762), *.home.arpa (RFC 8375), *.internal (reserved by ICANN in 2024; this covers host.docker.internal and metadata.google.internal). Match by suffix with the leading dot, compared in lowercase. (b) Parse as an IP address first. Only a host that is not an IP and contains no '.' becomes 不 under principle 2-a, with a new reason net_host_dotless. Doing the dotless check before the IP parse would turn bare IPv6 loopback http://[::1]/x, which is currently correctly 内, into 不. (c) Every other name stays external. A separate problem turned up while verifying and is outside this finding: '[::1]:8080' (IPv6 with a port) is misclassified as 矛 net_external_host, because the host is only split out when the string has at most one colon, so the whole '[::1]:8080' is kept as the host and does not parse as an IP. This is a false alarm in the same function and worth reporting as its own finding. The corpus counts in the finding ('http://gw:' 375 and so on) are raw string-literal counts that include tests and vendored code, and I have not verified them. Whether and how to define private for names is the student's decision, and it should not be made by looking at the counts.

Not refuted. I re-ran the repro and it reproduces. D4 gives no note (内) for NOTIFY, CALL, COPY, UPSERT and ATTACH. For the same kind of statement, D1 and D2 give 不 `db_unknown_statement`. `_d4` (dparse.py:419-430) does what the §7.4 row says: "DB: それ以外の先頭語 / 読み取り / 接続単位 → 内". But the finding does not misread the rule. It points out that the table disagrees with itself.

(1) §7 says it applies the §6 principles to §5 mechanically. §5 has no D4 row for heads outside the classification. §6 principle 2-a says a property that cannot be decided statically is 不. §7.5 says in general that "それ以外（ATTACH、NOTIFY、分類に無い PRAGMA など）→ 不". §7.1 and §7.2 both have the row "先頭語が分類に無い → 不". Only §7.4 lumps every other head into 内.

(2) The FS_WRITE row of §7.4 gives a reason for 内 ("2 回目は失敗する"). The DB row gives no reason why a head outside the classification would be idempotent. That reasoning plausibly covers the classified DELETE/DROP/CREATE/TRUNCATE/ALTER, but not unclassified heads. NOTIFY and COPY FROM add an effect on every call, so they cannot be derived as 内.

(3) Nothing records this as intended. I grepped decisions.md (D56, D57, D62), open_questions.md, review_plan.md §5/§7.5 and the D4 CASES in tests/test_contradiction_principles.py. None of them explains unclassified heads → 内 for D4. The D4 tests only check INSERT (不) and DELETE (内).

(4) The finding does not ask to add a sink, entry or weak reason. The fix only changes the DB row of §7.4 and uses the existing `sql_class` in `_d4`, so it is not a vocabulary addition. Under D62 and review_plan.md §7.5, D4 is now a primary metric, so this is no longer out of scope just because it only affects D4.

generality.reason:
This finding survives. The repro gives the claimed output: d4_notify, d4_call, d4_copy, d4_upsert and d4_attach come out as 内 with no note. The same statements under D1 / D2 (d1_notify, d2_call) come out as 不 `db_unknown_statement`. d4_executemany_insert is 不 `db_nonidempotent_statement`.

Design axis: the §7.4 row "DB: それ以外の先頭語 / 読み取り / 接続単位 → 内" is not a design decision. It is a derivation slip, and it contradicts three things written in the same §7:
- §7.5 closes with "それ以外（ATTACH、NOTIFY、分類に無い PRAGMA など）→ 不".
- Principle 2-a (§6) says a property that cannot be decided statically is 不.
- The docstring of `authgap/catalog/statements.py` says "ここに無いものは「不明」になる（原理 2-a）".

In §5, the only D4 × DB cell listed is #5 × INSERT → 2. Unclassified heads were never derived for D4. review_plan §5 does not list this as known, and D62 does not treat it as intended either. D62 only changed the standing of §7.3 / §7.4, and its §7.5 puts D3 / D4 errors in scope for fixing.

Generality axis: the natural fix is `sql_class(text, complete) == SQL_CLASS_UNKNOWN → 不` inside `_d4`. It comes from the language rule plus principle 2-a, not from tuning to v2 / v3. Controls run under verify/d3d4/r6_5 are currently 内 correctly and stay 内 after that fix, because their `sql_class` is not UNKNOWN: DELETE, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, VACUUM, `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` and SELECT. The only cases that change are unclassified PRAGMA assignments (e.g. `PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint = 1000`) and GRANT. Both are in fact idempotent and currently correct as 内, and the fix would turn them into 不. That is a move toward unknown, not a flip to 矛. It matches §7.5's "分類に無い PRAGMA → 不" and how D2 treats the same statement. So no counterexample breaks a correct case in the wrong direction.

design.reason:
This is not an intended design decision, and I found no record of it as a known limitation. It stands as a false-clean on D3.

(1) Design records: grepping decisions.md (the TRANSFER-arguments row of D17 revision 3 at L1701, K1–K7), open_questions.md, contradiction_principles.md §9.2 and preregistration turned up nothing about a constant absolute or network-path ref passed to urljoin. D17 revision 3 only covers the case where the non-subject arguments are non-literal ("drop the shape"). The all-literal branch (`Str((subject,))`, engine.py:918-919) keeps only the subject (BASE), and no decision says that is right for urljoin. §9.2 even states the reason for not producing false-clears on `//` with urljoin-style clients, so the design intent is on the finding's side.

(2) Re-deriving the expected output from §7.3: the destination of `urljoin("http://localhost:8000/api/", "https://api.example.com/x")` is `https://api.example.com/x`, a constant external host, so it should be 矛 `net_external_host`. The implementation says url.host='localhost:8000', `_host_class`=local, 内 (no row). The finding reads the rule correctly and the implementation does not follow it.

(3) This is not a request to add frozen vocabulary. It fixes how an existing TRANSFER row (urljoin) is evaluated.

(4) Re-run: the repro reproduces as described. I also confirmed that the network-path reference `urljoin("http://localhost:8000/api/", "//evil.example/x")` becomes url.host='localhost:8000', 内 (false-clean) (scratchpad verify/d3d4/r1d_r6_6). When BASE is a constant concatenation (a Str whose const is None), the result is `net_host_unknown`, 不 (no false-clean, only a count loss). When BASE contains the model's value, the result is `net_model_host`, 矛 (the verdict is correct).

Severity: code that passes a constant absolute URL to urljoin is rare, so I agree with low. Direction: false_clean, and it only affects D3. Since D62 made D3 a primary metric, this is in scope under §7.5.

The fix sketch (compute `urllib.parse.urljoin` when both the subject const and args[1] are literal str) also covers the network-path case. A somewhat more general alternative: when the literal ref has a scheme or starts with `//`, take the host from the ref regardless of whether BASE is constant.

generality.notes: General fix, restricted to the positive direction. In _host_class, when url.host has Seq/Argv shape, look at every element and the tail. Run each element through _split_url and classify its host with the existing Atom rule. If any element is a constant external host, return 'external' (矛 net_external_host). Otherwise, if any element is MODEL-chosen, or the Seq-level _choice is chosen, return 'model'; if influenced, return 'model_opaque'. Otherwise return 'unknown'. Do NOT return 'local' for a Seq, even when every visible element is a constant local host. Reason: Seq does not record list vs tuple, and list mutations through an alias, a callee, an unmodelled library or a container do not show up in the Seq. Those cases are now correctly 不 and would become false-clean 内 (counterexamples in scratchpad/verify/d3d4/r6_7b, verified with repro_scan.py). The finder's fix_sketch claim 'nothing correct breaks' is therefore wrong for its 'all local -> local' branch. The same aliasing gap also allows a rare false alarm in the external branch (e.g. a callee clears the list and refills it with localhost). That is the same trust the analyzer already gives to resolved Seq/Argv elements for argv0, so it is acceptable. A regression test should pin the 4 alias/callee/opaque/container forms as 不. On direction: 矛 -> 不 is a missed contradiction rather than a 内 clear. I kept false_clean to match how the finder labelled it; rule_mismatch would also be defensible.
